subject: Prompt: RL inference mini-project — deliverables, deadline & reviewer slots
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@gmail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prompt: RL inference mini-project — deliverables, deadline & reviewer slots

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for interviewing with the infra team last week. As discussed, attached is the mini take-home focused on inference behavior and latency-quality tradeoffs. High-level instructions below: 

- Deliverables: short write-up (max 2 pages), a small inference script showing your experiments, and results table/plots. Upload a single zip or share a Drive link.
- Starter artifacts: starter-dataset.csv (attached) + prompt PDF with details.
- Deadline: Monday, May 3, 2027 at 23:59 PT. If you need a short extension, let us know before the deadline.
- Allowed: standard Python libs, PyTorch or JAX, NumPy, matplotlib. No external network calls (offline run) — we’ll provide the trimmed model weights used in the prompt.
- Time expectation: ~3–6 hours for a concise submission.

How to submit: reply to this thread with the artifact or paste a Drive link. We’ll confirm receipt and schedule the review.

Review process: two reviewers from the infra team (we’ll assign Marissa and Priyom). Review window will be May 4–6; we’ll send calendar invites.

Attachments: RL-inference-prompt-2027-04.pdf (PDF, 5 pages), starter-dataset.csv (CSV, ~2MB).

Can you confirm you got this and the deadline works?

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Recruiting Lead — Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@gmail.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt: RL inference mini-project — deliverables, deadline & reviewer slots

Hi Markus —

Thanks — got the prompt and files. Deadline works for me. Quick question: when you say "no external network calls", does that rule out pulling pretrained checkpoints from public URLs during the run? I can download and vendor any required weights ahead of time if needed. Also — is it OK to use Hugging Face transformers for tokenization only?

I’ll start on this today.

Best,
Jordan

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@gmail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt: RL inference mini-project — deliverables, deadline & reviewer slots

Thanks for the quick reply, Jordan — confirmed.

To clarify: please do not make live network calls from the test run. If you need model weights, download and include them in your submission (or vendor a small trimmed checkpoint). Tokenizers from transformers for preprocessing are fine so long as the submitted package runs offline.

Marissa / Lauren — assigning reviewers: please confirm availability to review between May 4–6. If either of you needs different days, flag here and we’ll adjust.

Markus

Thanks for the ping — I can review and will be the primary reviewer. Priyom has also agreed to be the second reviewer (looping him now).

Slots I have open:
- Tue May 4, 9:00–11:00 PT (deep review)
- Wed May 5, 13:00–15:00 PT (follow-up discussion)

I’ll send a calendar invite with the primary review session and attach a lightweight ICS (review-slot-invite.ics). Please paste the submission link in this thread when Jordan uploads so reviewers have it pinned.

Marissa Cole
Senior Infra Engineer (Reviewer)
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear instructions and the quick review window — let me know if you need anything else.

Best,
